git_scope: Sparse checkout of the named files at the pinned commit for issue #506. Two commits follow 3ef7634, the issue-488 pin: f311f08 adds 308, 343 and 380 and changes 175, 340, 376, 378 and 379; 337078c adds 344 and 381 and changes 304, 305, 338, 339, 375, 376, 378, 379 and 380. Against 3ef7634 that is five certificates added and ten changed, and those 15 are retained as factual data. The other 53 certificates the commit holds are unchanged and pinned by digest against the copies the issue-476 and issue-488 packets retain. The two READMEs and the 15 changed decimal pose files are pinned by digest only. The rest of the tree, including the drawings, is pinned by the commit and was not retained or executed.
license: No licence file or reuse terms at the pin: the tree has no LICENSE, and neither README.md nor certificates/README.md states terms. The 15 changed certificates are retained as factual data under the owner decision of 2026-10-09 recorded in resources/web/known-best-packings/README.md (Retained Factual Data); prose is hash-pinned and not copied. certificates/README.md credits Evan Daniel's MIT-licensed exact contact solver, which does not license this bundle.
claims: Issue #506 reports s(304) <= 8964782973424250487190982671787/500000000000000000000000000000, printed rounded up to 12 decimals as 17.929565946849, an exact optimum from Evan Daniel's exact contact solver started from SQUISH's #500 Mondrian packing and improved by Evan Daniel's fq.

Issue #506 reports s(305) <= 3590093296427542454697714045223/200000000000000000000000000000, printed as 17.950466482138, an exact optimum from the same solver started from SQUISH's #500 Mondrian packing and improved by the author's search cycle with David Ellsworth's refine_packing, basin hopping and LP.

Issue #506 reports nine certificates beyond the n <= 324 case corpus, as author reports for the beyond-horizon list: 338, 339, 344, 376, 378, 379, 380 and 381, exact optima from the same solver, and 375, a rational witness of its decimal packing with centres dilated by 1 + 1e-11.

The two commits since 3ef7634 change four further certificates the issue does not name, each with its exact side and its side rounded up to 12 decimals in certificates/README.md: 175 and 308 in the case corpus, and 340 and 343 beyond it.
The checker statements (Evan Daniel's verify_cert.py and this repository's sqpack verify.py) are the author's; no optimality claim is made.
